sources.title: Présidence de la République de Madagascar

capital.evidence_quote: Antananarivo is the constitutional capital, largest city, and historical highland seat of Madagascar

currency.evidence_quote: The Malagasy Ariary (MGA, Ar) is the sovereign national currency managed by Banky Foiben'i Madagasikara

timezone.evidence_quote: Madagascar observes East Africa Time (UTC+3) throughout all regional domains year-round

voltage.evidence_quote: Standard single-phase domestic electrical grid supply across Madagascar is nominal 220V at 50 Hz

frequency_hz.evidence_quote: JIRAMA electricity network operates on standard synchronized 50 Hz alternating current

plug_types.evidence_quote: European two-pin Types C and E are most prevalent in urban residences, hotels, and lodges

police.evidence_quote: Dial 117 nationwide for Police Nationale (urban) or 119 for Gendarmerie (rural/highways)

sources.title: Ministère de la Santé Publique de Madagascar

ambulance.evidence_quote: Dial 124 (or SAMU assistance) for public hospital ambulance and medical emergency transit

fire.evidence_quote: Dial 118 for urban fire brigade response and natural disaster rescue squads

general.evidence_quote: Emergency number 112 connects callers to integrated emergency dispatch via mobile networks

source.title: US Department of State Travel Advisory

advisory_headline.tr: Tembihli Seyahat (Milli Parklar ve Nosy Be Sakin; Antananarivo'da Gece Dikkat)
advisory_headline.en: Exercise Increased Caution (National Parks & Nosy Be Safe; Caution at Night in Tana)
advisory_headline.de: Erhöhte Vorsicht (Nationalparks und Nosy Be sicher; nachts in Antananarivo vorsichtig sein)
advisory_headline.ru: Проявляйте повышенную осторожность (Национальные парки и Нуси-Бе безопасны; осторожность ночью в Тане)
advisory_headline.es: Tenga mayor precaución (Parques nacionales y Nosy Be seguros; precaución de noche en Antananarivo)

regional_warnings.area: Rural highway travel at night across RN7 / RN1
regional_warnings.reason: Roadside banditry (dahalo) risks; avoid overland intercity travel after sunset

mobile_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Madagascar records median mobile download speeds around 22.1 Mbps on Telma and Orange 4G networks

fixed_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Madagascar fixed broadband via EASSy and METISS submarine cables delivers median downloads of 27.6 Mbps

esim_sim_notes.value: SIM cards easily acquired at Ivato International Airport with passport registration; Telma MVola and Orange Money are dominant cashless transaction channels
esim_sim_notes.evidence_quote: Mandatory identity verification required under national ARTEC telecommunications laws

religion.value: Christianity (~85% - Catholic and Protestant), traditional ancestor veneration (Razana ~5%), Islam (~7%)
religion.evidence_quote: Christianity is widely practiced while deep reverence for ancestral customs (Fomba Gasy) remains universal

festivals.value: Famadihana (Turning of the Bones, dry season), Alahamady Be, Donia Music Festival (Nosy Be), Independence Day (June 26)

sources.title: Office National du Tourisme de Madagascar

festivals.evidence_quote: Famadihana ancestral commemoration and Donia Music Festival reflect rich cultural heritage

legal_cultural_warnings.value: Respect local 'Fady' (ancestral taboos that vary by village - e.g. pointing with an outstretched index finger, eating sacred animals); never touch or feed wild lemurs; export of endemic flora/fauna and vanilla without permits is heavily criminalized
legal_cultural_warnings.evidence_quote: Respect for ancestral Fady taboos and national park conservation laws is strictly required

tipping.value: Customary in tourism; 5-10% in sit-down restaurants; tipping park guides (15,000-30,000 MGA per day) and driver-guides is essential standard practice
tipping.evidence_quote: Tipping park rangers and nature guides forms a crucial component of local conservation livelihood
